title: Build CogniCare
subtitle: The complete assembly guide, from bare aluminium to a working robot.
intro:
CogniCare is a desktop-sized humanoid robot: a pan-and-tilt head with two display eyes, speakers and a visor, a 16-inch touchscreen, and a full **ITX PC** inside a rotating base.

This guide follows the assembly animation step by step. Scroll and the video plays each step; every printed part has a 3D preview you can spin.
notes:
- **Test every servo first** and give it its ID: **1** = hip, **4** = tilt, **5** = pan. Then put them in servo mode at position **500** so nothing moves unexpectedly.
- Print every part in the **same brand** of PLA so the colour matches.
- Drive screws at about **1 Nm** with the drill's clutch, then finish by hand so you don't crack printed parts.
- Nearly every fastener is **M5**, going into drop-in T-nuts in the 2020 profiles. All outer panels (the base's acrylic boards and the nine body panels) fix with **M5 countersunk screws**.
- Every printed part is **white Creality Hyper PLA**. Print every **gear** at **70 % infill**.
- **Plan your cables early.** Everything from the upper body leaves through the umbilical cord port on the back and plugs into the I/O panel on the base. Leave slack so the hip can rotate without yanking cables.

steps.title: Cut the 340 mm profiles
steps.text: Cut **four 340 mm** lengths of 2020 aluminium profile. You need two now; the other two close the top of the base in step 27.
steps.tip: Clamp the bars together and deburr the ends so every length matches.

steps.title: Add the 3-way corner brackets
steps.text: Fit a 3-way corner bracket to both ends of the two 340 mm profiles, using the screws supplied with the brackets. The upright arm of each bracket points **up**: the corner posts slot onto it in step 9.

steps.title: Close the bottom rectangle
steps.text: Cut **four 310 mm** profiles. Join two of them between the bracketed 340 mm profiles to make a rectangle. Keep the other two for the top frame.

steps.title: Lower frame done
steps.text: The bottom rectangle of the base is complete. Tighten every bracket screw.
steps.tip: Measure both diagonals: if they match, the frame is square.

steps.title: Laser-cut the lower board
steps.text: Cut the **Lower Board** from 3 mm acrylic.

steps.title: Fit the lower board supports
steps.text: Print **Lower Board Support 1** and **Lower Board Support 2** and lay them on top of the acrylic. They spread the load so the board doesn't scratch or crack when the robot is moved.

steps.title: Add the feet
steps.text: Print **four Feet**, line them up under the corners and fix them with M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts.

steps.title: Flip the frame
steps.text: Turn the frame over so it stands on its feet.

steps.title: Stand up the corner posts
steps.text: Cut **four 118 mm** profiles and push one onto the upright arm of each 3-way bracket. Tighten with a hex key.

steps.title: Mount the PSU holder
steps.text:
The base houses a full **ITX PC**. If you use a Jetson, a NUC or another computer you'll need your own mounts; the rest of the build stays the same.

Print the **Power Supply Holder That Connects with Aluminium Profile** and fix it in one corner with M5 × 10 mm socket screws and drop-in T-nuts. The PSU's power inlet must face a **340 mm** profile.

prints.part: Power Supply Holder That Connects with Aluminium Profile

steps.warning: The holder fits ATX supplies up to 125 × 150 × 86 mm (made for the Corsair CX650).

steps.title: Install the power supply
steps.text: Slide the PSU into the holder and screw it in with the screws from the PSU box. We used a **Corsair CX650** (650 W, 80+ Bronze). Any unit of the same size with **non-modular** cables will do.

steps.title: Add the PSU exhaust guide
steps.text: Print the **PSU Exhust Air Guide** and fit it over the PSU's exhaust grille. It sends hot air out of the base instead of letting it circulate back in. Fix it with one countersunk screw and a drop-in T-nut.

steps.title: Cover the PSU intake
steps.text: Print the **PSU Shield** and tape (or lightly glue) it over the PSU's intake. It stops screws and debris falling into the PSU while you build.

steps.title: Next: the motherboard
steps.text: Power is in place. Next comes the motherboard.

steps.title: Print the motherboard base
steps.text: Print the **Motherboard Base** and melt **M3 heat-set inserts** into its four mounting holes. Bolt it to the 340 mm profile with M5 countersunk screws, keeping the spacing below so the motherboard's I/O lines up with the side panel.

images.caption: Distance Between Motherboard Base and the 118mm Profile

steps.title: Add the motherboard supports
steps.text: Print **Motherboard Support Left** and **Motherboard Support Right** and join them to the base with M5 countersunk screws and nuts (M5 inserts work too). They hold the far end of the board so it can't sag. Leave their **top ends free**: they bolt to the top frame in step 27.

steps.title: Fit the motherboard
steps.text: Screw the ITX motherboard, with CPU and cooler already fitted, onto the inserts. Use a **low-profile cooler** so it fits under the top frame.
steps.tip: Fit the CPU, cooler, RAM and SSD on the bench first. It's much harder once the board is in the base.

steps.title: Snap on the fan guard
steps.text: Print the **120mm Cooling Fan Gurd Mainly for CPU Cooler Fans**. It snap-fits over the cooler fan.

prints.part: 120mm Cooling Fan Gurd Mainly for CPU Cooler Fans

steps.title: Next: the GPU
steps.text: The motherboard is done. Now the graphics card.

steps.title: Print the GPU holder
steps.text: Print **GPU Holder Main**. Melt **M3 inserts** into the two small holes and **M5 inserts** into the larger ones. Then screw the slot end of the PCIe riser into the lower part.

downloads.name: Cooler Master PCIe 4.0 x16 300mm Riser Cable

files.step: Cooler Master PCIe 4.0 x16 300mm Riser Cable.step
files.stl: Cooler Master PCIe 4.0 x16 300mm Riser Cable.stl
files.f3d: Cooler Master PCIe 4.0 x16 300mm Riser Cable.f3d

steps.title: Fit the GPU mounting parts
steps.text: Print **GPU Holder Mounting Parts**. Of its four holes, bolt the **centre two** to the GPU's bracket, matching the wedge on the print to the bracket.
steps.warning: Use a **low-profile GPU** fitted with its small-form-factor bracket. We used a Gigabyte RTX 3050 OC Low Profile 6 GB.
components: Gigabyte RTX 3050 OC Low Profile 6 GB

steps.title: Seat the GPU
steps.text: Push the GPU into the riser's PCIe slot and check it's fully seated. The outer side of the mounting part lines up with the M5 inserts in **GPU Holder Main**: fix it there with M5 × 10 mm screws.

steps.title: Add the GPU support
steps.text: Print **GPU Holder Additional Support** and bolt it on with M5 screws and hex nuts. It locks the card in place so it can't work loose in transport.

steps.title: Mount the GPU assembly
steps.text: Lower the whole GPU assembly into the base and fix it to the 310 mm profiles with M5 countersunk screws. Before tightening the screws, push it **as close as possible to the 340 mm profiles**. Leave room for the HDMI cable.

steps.title: Install the case fan
steps.text: One 120 mm fan cools the base. Screw it to the printed **Fan Mount With Aluminium Profile**, then fix the mount to the lower 310 mm profile with M5 countersunk screws. Fit **only the lower screws** for now; the top profile isn't on yet.

images.caption: Distance between the Fan Mount and the 118mm Profile

steps.title: Add the fan inlet guide
steps.text: Print the **120mm Fan Inlet Air Guide** and fit it in front of the fan with two M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts. The fan is an **intake**, and the guide makes it pull fresh air from outside instead of re-breathing warm air from inside the base.

steps.title: Close the top of the base
steps.text:
Build a second rectangle from the remaining **two 310 mm** and **two 340 mm** profiles with 3-way brackets and set it on the corner posts.

Now fit the screws you left out earlier: the two at the top of the motherboard supports and the top screw of the fan mount.

steps.title: Build the front I/O module
steps.text: Print **Power Menu Connector Top Part** (melt in an M5 insert) and **Power Menu Connector Lower Part**. Clamp the front-panel board (power button, audio and USB) between them.
steps.tip: Ours came from a DeepCool CH170 case. A different front panel needs its own holder.

steps.title: Mount the front I/O
steps.text: Fix the I/O module to the top 340 mm profile with M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts.

images.caption: Distance between Power Menu Connector Top and the 118mm Profile

steps.title: Add the backplate cover
steps.text: Print the **Motherboard Backplate** cover. It sits over the motherboard and leaves a clear path for hot air to escape. Fix it with two M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts.

images.caption: Distance Between Motherboard Back Plate and the 118mm Profile

steps.title: Wire the PC
steps.text: Connect the CPU, GPU and PSU cables now. The outer panels go on next and make access much harder.
steps.tip: Power it on once and check everything works before closing it up. Having someone experienced check your cable routing helps. Keep the motherboard's I/O side clear. The cables coming down from the robot's body plug in there later.
components: PSU cables: 24-pin ATX, 8-pin CPU, PCIe power

steps.title: Cut the I/O side panel
steps.text: Laser-cut the **Right Board (Motherboard IO Side)** from 3 mm acrylic. It has a cut-out for the GX16 connector.

steps.title: Mount the GX16 socket
steps.text: Print the **GX 16 Holder** and fix the **male GX16-3** connector in it with its own nut. Then bolt the holder to the panel with M5 screws and nuts.

steps.title: Fit the I/O side panel
steps.text:
Print two **Screw Support for Board Small**, lay them along the panel edge and fix the panel to the frame with four M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts.

Then add the printed **Updated GPU Backplate v1** with the same screws and nuts.
steps.warning: Wire the GX16 connector **before** closing up. It carries mains power from the emergency stop you'll fit later.

steps.title: Fit the back panel
steps.text: Laser-cut the **Back Board** and **Front Board**. Fix the back board to the frame with the **Screw Support for Board Large**.

steps.title: Fit the left panel & power inlet
steps.text:
Laser-cut the **Left Board** and press-fit the printed **AC Power Enter Hole** into it.

Two mains cables pass through here: one powers the PC, the other runs through the emergency stop to the GX16 socket. Leave both long.

steps.title: Fit the front panel
steps.text: Fix the **Front Board** with **Screw Support for Board Small**, four M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts.

steps.title: Add the inner 310 mm rails
steps.text:
Cut **two more 310 mm** profiles and fit them inside the top frame with **corner brackets**, M5 screws and drop-in T-nuts. Keep **66 mm between outer faces** and **26 mm between inner faces** to the neighbouring profile.

This spacing needs to be as accurate as possible, so use **Aluminium Profile Spacing Measurement Helper 1** and **Aluminium Profile Spacing Measurement Helper 2** to space the two profiles exactly.
steps.tip: Remove the spacing helpers once the screws are tight.

steps.title: Add the 218 mm cross rails
steps.text: Cut **two 218 mm** profiles and join them to the inner rails with corner brackets, keeping the same **26 mm / 66 mm** spacing. Use the dimensions from step 38 to place the profiles accurately.

steps.title: Fit the components protector
steps.text: Print the **Protector for PC Components** and fix it with M5 screws and drop-in T-nuts. Its many holes make cable management easy.
steps.warning: Match the orientation shown in the animation: the **flat side** of the Protector for PC Components faces the **PSU and cooling fan** side.

steps.title: Lay the top board
steps.text: Laser-cut the **Top Board** and lay it on the frame. The **square cut-out** must sit on the GPU/fan side: the emergency-stop cable is routed through it.

steps.title: Top supports & emergency stop
steps.text:
Print four **Top Board Screw Support** and fix the top board with M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts.

Print the **Emergency Switch Holder**, mount the **AB6-A emergency stop** and solder its wires:

- One 220 V cable feeds the PSU directly.
- A second 220 V cable enters through the AC inlet, runs through the emergency stop and on to the GX16 socket.
steps.warning: This is **mains voltage**. Insulate every joint with heat-shrink and test with the plug out.

steps.title: Add the main body lifters
steps.text: Print four **Updated Main Body Lifter Support** and fix one in each corner inside the top frame with countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts.

steps.title: Print the motor bearing holder
steps.text: Print one **Lazy Susan Bearing Holder with Servo Motor**. It carries the hip motor.

prints.part: Lazy Susan Bearing Holder with Servo Motor

steps.title: Fit the hip servo
steps.text: Fit a **Hiwonder HTD-85H** (the version with the round output shaft) into the holder and secure it with the six screws under the servo.
steps.tip: Set this servo's ID to **1** before you build it in.

steps.title: Add the hip driver gear
steps.text: Print the **Hip Driver Gear** at **70 % infill** and fix it to the servo shaft with the screws supplied with the HTD-85H.

steps.title: Print the second bearing holder
steps.text: Print one **Lazy Susan Bearing Holder Without Motor**.

prints.part: Lazy Susan Bearing Holder Without Motor

steps.title: Mount the lazy-susan bearing
steps.text:
Lay the **10-inch lazy-susan bearing** over both holders: they line up with its outer ring. Join them with long screws.

T-nut slots at the holder ends let you unbolt the whole upper robot (hip to head) whenever you like and park it on the printed **Robot Temporary Base During Transportation**.
steps.tip: To fix the robot permanently, set the holders in the profile beside the main body lifters and bolt them down with T-nuts and M5 screws.

steps.title: Rest it on the base
steps.text: Set the bearing assembly into the profile slots. Don't fix it yet: many screws still have to go in.

steps.title: Stack the hip layers
steps.text:
Stack these over the bearing, lining up the four holes:

1. **Inner Driven Gear of Hip**: print at 70 % infill
2. **Mesh Protecting Part**
3. **Core Support**

Bolt all the layers together with M5 screws from the top and M5 hex nuts underneath.
steps.tip: The gear fits the bearing very tightly. That's intentional.

steps.title: Raise the core profiles
steps.text: Four 2020 profiles carry the whole upper body: **343 mm at the front** and **393 mm at the back**. Seat them in the **Core Support**, making sure each profile sits fully inside its hole, and fix them with M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts. The four outer holes are enough; the inner ones are spare.

steps.title: Mount the 12 V servo supply
steps.text:
The **12 V 10 A SMPS** powers the servos.

- Wire it first: a **long** AC lead (it ends in a GX16 female plug that connects to the base) and a **short** DC lead (the servo controller sits right on top).
- Fix **12V SMPS Holder Lower Part** at the cable end using the supply's M3 holes (or its slots with M3 nuts), then fit **12V SMPS Holder Upper Part**.
- Mount the assembly on the **back** (longer) profiles with M5 countersunk screws and drop-in T-nuts, leaving the 1 mm clearance shown.
- Stick the **Hiwonder BusLinker V3.0** to the upper holder with double-sided tape.
components: Long AC lead (to the GX16 plug)

images.caption: Distance between SMPS Holder Lower and Core Support

steps.warning: **Plan the cable route before you wire anything in the body.** Every cable from the upper body (servo bus, 12 V supply, eye displays, speakers, camera, microphone) runs down the back core profiles, out through the **Right Umbilical Cord Hole** in the **Rear Section with Umbilical Cord Hole** and into the **I/O panel** on the side of the base. Keep that path clear, and leave a generous slack loop between body and base so nothing gets yanked when the hip rotates.

steps.title: Fit the lower panel connectors
steps.text: Print **Left Lower Generated Connector** and **Right Lower Generated Connector** at **40 % infill** or more. Press M5 hex nuts into every hex slot; a drop of super glue keeps them there. Fix one to each side of the core with M5 screws and drop-in T-nuts.

images.caption: Distance between Left Lower Connection and Core Support

steps.title: Build the display mount
steps.text: The mount is made for a **ViewSonic TD1655**. For a different screen, only the holder needs redesigning. Print **Display Connector with Core Profiles - Lower**, **Display Connector with Core Profiles - Upper** and the **ViewSonic TD1655 Display Holder**, and join them with M5 × 25 mm countersunk screws and hex nuts.

prints.part: Display Connector with Core Profiles - Lower
Display Connector with Core Profiles - Upper

steps.tip: Leave the lower two holes empty. They're reserved for future add-ons.

steps.title: Install the display mount
steps.text: Take the SMPS assembly off, then slide the display mount down over the core profiles from the top. Fix all four sides with M5 flat-head screws and drop-in T-nuts.

images.caption: Distance between Display Connector Lower, Upper and the Core Support

steps.warning: The SMPS assembly has to be removed first: the display mount can't slot in past it. Refit the SMPS once the mount is fixed.

steps.title: Add a wire guide
steps.text: Print the small **Wire Guide - Small Version** and fit it at any convenient spot on the two back profiles. Zip-tie cables through its holes.

steps.title: Fit the neck base
steps.text: Print the **Entire Head Support and Neck Pan Motor Holder**, slide it onto the core profiles from the top and fix it with M5 flat-head screws and drop-in T-nuts. Its servo mount faces the robot's **left**.

prints.part: Entire Head Support and Neck Pan Motor Holder

images.caption: Neck base offset from the aluminium profiles

steps.title: Fit the upper panel connectors
steps.text: Print **Left Upper Generated Connector** and **Right Upper Generated Connector** at **40 % infill** or more. Press M5 hex nuts into the hex slots (a drop of super glue helps) and fix one to each side of the core with M5 screws and drop-in T-nuts.

images.caption: Left Right Upper Generated Connector Distance From Top of Profile 1
Left Right Upper Generated Connector Distance From Top of Profile 2

steps.title: Build the pan drive
steps.text: Fit an **HX-35HM** servo with its round horn and screw the printed **Neck Pan Gear Driver** (70 % infill) onto it.
steps.tip: This is the **pan** servo: give it ID **5**.

steps.title: Install the pan servo
steps.text: Drop the servo into its slot and fix it with the screws from underneath.
steps.tip: If it wobbles, wrap a little PTFE or Scotch tape around it.

steps.title: Stack the pan bearing
steps.text:
Press the **6007 bearing** into place, then stack:

1. **Support for Neck Pan Gear Driven** (60 % infill)
2. **Neck Pan Gear Driven** (70 % infill)
3. **Neck Pan and Tilt Part Connection** (40 % infill)

Four long screws from the top of the connector hold the stack. They thread straight into the plastic, so no nuts are needed. The hole through the bearing centre carries one servo cable.

prints.part: Support for Neck Pan Gear Driven
Neck Pan and Tilt Part Connection

steps.warning: The snug fit on the 6007 bearing carries the whole head. If it's loose, add PTFE tape until it's tight.

steps.title: Build the tilt drive
steps.text: Fit a second **HX-35HM** with its round horn and screw on the printed **Neck Tilt Gear Driver** (70 % infill).
steps.tip: This is the **tilt** servo: give it ID **4**.

steps.title: Install the tilt servo
steps.text: Fit the tilt servo into its slot in the Neck Pan and Tilt Part Connection and screw it in. Then connect all the servos to the BusLinker.
steps.tip: Feed the pan servo's cable through the hole in the 6007 bearing, then down the back profiles. Leave enough slack for the head to pan and tilt through its full range.

steps.title: Press in the tilt bearings
steps.text: Press a **6804-2RS bearing** into each side of the Neck Pan and Tilt Part Connection.

steps.title: Left head joint & tilt gear
steps.text: Fit the **Neck Tilt Left Head Joint** into the left bearing (left from the robot's point of view). Bolt the **Neck Tilt Gear Driven** (70 % infill) to it with long M5 flat-head screws and M5 nuts in the hex slots.

steps.title: Right head joint
steps.text: Fit the **Neck Tilt Right Head Joint** into the right bearing.

steps.title: Bridge the head joints
steps.text: Print the **Left Right Head Joint Connector** at **60 % infill** and join the two joints with M5 flat-head screws and nuts. There are six holes, but four screws are enough. The left side is a tight squeeze.

steps.title: Add the head pivots
steps.text: Print the **Head Front Connector** and **Head Back Connector** and fix them to the bridge with M5 screws and hex nuts.
steps.tip: Glue the hex nuts into the back pivot's slots so they stay put.

steps.title: Print the head front
steps.text: Print the **Head Front with Ribs** at **40 % infill**, front face down on the bed, with plenty of supports. Sand it smooth afterwards.
steps.warning: Print orientation matters here: face down, fully supported.

steps.title: Add the head inserts
steps.text: Melt **M5 heat-set inserts** into the holes in the **Head Front with Ribs**. Most head parts screw into them.

steps.title: Make the visor
steps.text:
The visor is a curved sheet of 2–2.5 mm clear acrylic.

1. Print the **Eye Glass or Visor** part (it is the mould).
2. Heat the acrylic with a heat gun and press it over the mould (a thin cloth in between avoids marks).
3. Trim it to shape and glue it to the printed **Visor Holder**.
steps.warning: Don't use super glue on acrylic. It fogs the surface.

steps.title: Mount the visor
steps.text: Screw the visor assembly to the head with M5 × 12 mm countersunk screws.

steps.title: Build the speakers
steps.text: Print the **Left Speaker Holder** and **Right Speaker Holder** and fix a 52 mm driver in each with M4 screws. Ours are the 3 W drivers from a Havit SK717; any driver that fits will do.
components: Speaker amplifier board (from the Havit SK717)

steps.title: Mount the first speaker
steps.text: Screw the speaker into the inserts inside the head with 12 mm M5 screws. Use 25 mm screws in the two holes it shares with the display holder.

steps.title: Mount the second speaker
steps.text: Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Install the eye displays
steps.text: Two **4-inch HDMI displays** form the eyes. Print the **Left Display Holder** and **Right Display Holder**, fix the displays in with glue or double-sided tape (HDMI port towards the cut-out), then push each holder into place and screw it in.
steps.tip: One display screw shares a hole with the speaker, so you may need to take the speaker holder off first. Dark filament and a tinted visor look great here.
steps.warning: Use **soft, flexible** HDMI and USB cables. Stiff cables fight the head as it moves.

steps.title: Join the head to the pivot
steps.text: Attach the head assembly to the **Head Front Connector** with four 12 mm M5 countersunk screws.

steps.title: Build the head back
steps.text: Print the **Head Back** and the **Head Top Camera Holder** and join them with M5 countersunk screws and hex nuts. The cover closes the hole on top. Swap it out if you add a head camera later.

steps.title: Close the head
steps.text: Fix the **Head Back** to the **Head Back Connector** and the **Head Front with Ribs** with 16 mm M5 countersunk screws.

steps.title: Route the head cables
steps.text: Run all the head cables down into the body through the opening behind the neck. Tilt the head through its full range to check nothing snags, then zip-tie them.
steps.tip: Carry on down the same path: behind the neck, along the back core profiles, to the umbilical cord port. Leave slack at the neck **and** above the hip.

steps.title: Print the nine body panels
steps.text: Nine panels make the outer shell. Start them early: they're the longest prints in the build. Each one fixes to the panel connectors with **16 mm M5 countersunk screws** into the hex nuts.

prints.part: Rear Section with Umbilical Cord Hole

steps.title: Fit the Lower Midsection
steps.text: Fit the **Lower Midsection** first.

steps.title: Fit the Midsection
steps.text: Then the **Midsection** above it.

steps.title: Fit the Left Hole Filler With LEDs
steps.text: Print the **Left Hole Filler With LEDs** and fix it into the left opening of the **Rear Section with Umbilical Cord Hole** with M5 countersunk screws and hex nuts.

steps.title: Fit the Right Umbilical Cord Hole
steps.text: Fit the **Right Umbilical Cord Hole** into the right opening the same way. Every cable from the upper body leaves through here to the base.
steps.tip: Pass every upper-body cable through this port before you fit it, then run them into the base's I/O panel. Leave a slack loop here so the hip can turn without pulling on anything.

steps.title: Attach the Rear Section with Umbilical Cord Hole
steps.text: Fix the assembled **Rear Section with Umbilical Cord Hole** to the robot with M5 countersunk screws.

steps.text: Fit the **Astra Camera Holder**, designed for an Astra depth camera.

steps.title: Mount the display
steps.text:
Slide the TD1655's aluminium back plate into the display mount.

Optional: print the **Monitor Magnetic Mount For Microphone And Additional Small Camera**, press in 8 × 7 mm neodymium magnets with a drop of glue, and clip a Boya BY-M1 microphone into it on top of the screen.

prints.part: Monitor Magnetic Mount For Microphone And Additional Small Camera

steps.title: CogniCare is complete
steps.text: Connect everything and test it: the servos, the eye animation and the camera. Then enjoy your robot.
